references.text: The Lord God sends me with his Spirit, just as Jesus emphasizes that the Father who sent him is with him and has not left him alone.
Isaiah describes the Messiah as one who listens and does God's will, paralleling Jesus' claim that he always does what is pleasing to the Father.
Jesus explains earlier in the same Gospel that the Son can do nothing on his own, but only what he sees the Father doing, confirming that the Father is with him.
Jesus confirms that the Father is in him and performs his works, which is a direct extension of the claim that he is not alone because he always does God's will.
In his solemn prayer, Jesus affirms that he completed the work the Father gave him to do, which is the ultimate confirmation that he always did what was pleasing to him.
